newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan rethinks law to allow U.S. mutual insurer.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan rethinks law to allow U.S. mutual insurer.

text.p: Taipei, in trade talks with the United States about joining the World Trade Organisation (WTO), said on Wednesday it would reinterpret its laws to allow U.S. insurance firm Blue Cross Blue Shield to enter Taiwan.
The Board of Foreign Trade said it could approve the branch within a month if the mutual insurance company launches a formal application, as expected.

"We have agreed that if Blue Cross Blue Shield can set up a formal branch office in Taiwan, it could circumvent current legal difficulties regarding mutual insurance companies," a board official said.
Many foreign insurers have long operated in Taiwan, but U.S. mutual insurance firms, which have a cooperative ownership structure, have been blocked by a lack of explicit authorising regulations.

Taipei agreed to the liberalisation during talks between U.S. and Taiwan trade representatives regarding the island's long-frustrated bid to join the WTO. The two-day negotiation in Taipei ends on Wednesday.
Taiwan's foreign trade board said mutual insurance firms could circumvent the legal snag by registering a full subsidiary on the island.
"We do not intend to change our laws, but there are ways to interpret them to make them favourable towards liberalisation," the board official said.
The United States is one of eight WTO members with whom Taiwan still must complete bilateral negotiations to clear the way for its entry to the world trade body.
Taiwan has progressively liberalised many markets in its zeal to enter the WTO but faces a daunting political obstacle as long as rival China's WTO bid remains stalled.
Beijing insists that it must accede before Taipei.
